semanticDifferences: Field.Label is the part that registers the label id the control points at with aria-labelledby, and it derives htmlFor from the registered control (LabelableProvider.controlId). React Aria's Label got the same wiring from RAC's LabelContext, which TextField/NumberField/Select fed with react-aria's labelProps. Element, classes and text content are unchanged.

Field.Description publishes its id through LabelableProvider.setMessageIds; Field.Control merges those ids into aria-describedby (useFieldValidation.getValidationProps -> getDescriptionProps). React Aria's Text inherited descriptionProps/errorMessageProps from RAC's TextContext slots instead.

Field parts must be inside Field.Root: FieldLabel and FieldDescription both call useFieldRootContext(false), which throws 'Base UI: FieldRootContext is missing. Field parts must be placed within <Field.Root>' (error 28 in production). Both payload components therefore branch on the field context: Field.Label / Field.Description inside a Base UI field, an identical-class <label> / <span> outside it, which is how the 43 importers that render them standalone (select-native, pin-input, ...) keep working.

There is no public export for the default field context (internals/field-root-context exports FieldRootContext and useFieldRootContext only), so 'is there a Field.Root above?' is answered with Base UI's own missing-context sentinel: useFieldRootContext(true).setValidityData !== NOOP. Both subpaths are entries of the package's exports map (@base-ui/react/internals/field-root-context, @base-ui/react/internals/noop) and are pinned to 1.8.0 with the rest of @base-ui/react.

Field.Root (and Field.Item) are the only providers of the label/description context. NumberField/OTPField/Select/Combobox/Checkbox/Radio/Switch only consume it, so a payload Label inside one of those families associates with its control only when the owning component wraps it in Field.Root - the composition Base UI documents for those families.

Field.Description renders a

by default, which would change the hint's element and its inline/block participation. It is rendered through render={} so the hint stays the React Aria's Text rendered, while keeping the description id registration and the field data-* attributes.

Field.Error is deliberately not used for the isInvalid branch: it mounts only while the field reports invalid and swaps its children for the field's own validity message, which would hide the payload's always-rendered hint text (the payload decides when to render <HintText isInvalid>). HintText therefore uses Field.Description for both the description and the error message, exactly as RAC's Text carried both ids.

React Aria wired the control's aria-describedby only when the field was invalid; Field.Description registers the hint id in both states, so the hint is now programmatically associated in the valid state too - a superset of the previous association.

State is exposed as Base UI data-* attributes (data-invalid/data-disabled/data-filled/...) instead of React Aria's data-rac + data-* pairs; Label and HintText keep their own data-label/class vocabulary and the label/hint themselves now carry data-invalid/data-disabled/data-filled when they sit inside a Field.Root.

migrationRecord.existingUntitledUiBehavior: Label renders a <label> flex row (text-sm font-medium text-secondary) carrying data-label="true" (used by the `label` custom variant and `**:data-label:` selectors), a conditional brand/error `*` asterisk, and an optional Tooltip + TooltipTrigger with an icon; it accepted htmlFor/id and inherited RAC's field label wiring. HintText renders a <span> (text-sm text-tertiary, size sm -> text-xs, in-data-[input-size=sm]:text-xs) that doubles as the field's description or error message through RAC's slot="description"/"errorMessage" text context.
migrationRecord.canonicalBehavioralContract: label element associated with the field control (htmlFor + control aria-labelledby), required/invalid state driving the asterisk (explicit props first, field state as fallback), data-label preserved for conditional visibility CSS, hint rendered unconditionally with the same element/classes, and the hint identified to the control as its description; both components usable with no surrounding field component at all.
migrationRecord.baseUiCompositionChosen: Field.Label inside Field.Root; Field.Description (render={<span />}) inside Field.Root; the same <label>/<span> with identical classes when no Field.Root is above. Presence of the field context is detected with Base UI's own sentinel (useFieldRootContext(true).setValidityData !== NOOP).
migrationRecord.whyNotOneToOne: Base UI's Field parts have no standalone mode - they read (and require) Field.Root - while React Aria's Label/Text were plain elements that picked up a field context only if one existed. The dual rendering is the only faithful mapping of 'works inside a field, works alone' onto the Field split of Root/Label/Description; Field.Error is not the isInvalid counterpart because it is a validity-driven, conditionally mounted message rather than a caller-rendered hint.

publicApiChanges.before: string | ((state: LabelRenderProps | TextRenderProps) => string) (React Aria DOMRenderProps)
publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI resolves className per part from its own state object (render props are (props, state) => element, not a className function); neither component used render-prop state, and Base UI's state object is a different shape from React Aria's.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: Pass a string; Base UI's own className function form remains available through the parts if a consumer ever needs state-based classes.
publicApiChanges.compatibility: compile-time narrowing only: all 43 importers pass string literals or cx(...) results; payload typecheck passes.

publicApiChanges.before: ReactNode | ((state: LabelRenderProps | TextRenderProps) => ReactNode) (React Aria DOMRenderProps)
publicApiChanges.reason: Same render-prop removal as className; the payload renders element children only (Label additionally appends the asterisk and the tooltip trigger).
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: Render-prop children were never used by the payload; no behaviour change at any call site.
publicApiChanges.compatibility: compile-time narrowing only; payload typecheck passes.

publicApiChanges.before: string (inherited from React Aria's LabelProps/TextProps; e.g. elementType="span")
publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI parts render a fixed default element and swap it through the `render` prop, not an elementType prop.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: Label always renders <label> (required for Field.Label's native association), HintText always renders <span> (React Aria's default).
publicApiChanges.compatibility: no payload consumer passes elementType; payload typecheck passes.

publicApiChanges.before: slot={isInvalid ? "errorMessage" : "description"} consumed by React Aria's TextContext and rendered as a DOM slot attribute
publicApiChanges.after: no longer set internally; a consumer-passed slot would render as an inert DOM attribute
publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI has no slot routing: the hint is associated with the control by Field.Description registering its id in the field's message ids, which Field.Control merges into aria-describedby.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: The description/error association now follows from being inside a Field.Root rather than from the slot name; isInvalid keeps its styling meaning (text-error-primary).
publicApiChanges.compatibility: the only slot usage was HintText's own; no payload consumer and no stylesheet targets [slot=...] (checked in registry + styles).

stateSelectorChanges.reason: compiled to .group:is(:where([data-rac])[data-invalid], :where(:not([data-rac])):invalid) *: the data branch needed React Aria's data-rac on the group element and the native branch needs the group element itself to be natively :invalid, which a wrapper <div>/<span> never is. Base UI emits data-invalid on Field.Root and on its controls, so the attribute variant is the live one (verified in a browser: asterisk turns error-coloured from the wrapper's data-invalid alone).
same rewrite; the hint colour now follows data-invalid on the field wrapper, which Field.Root/NumberField.Root/Select.Trigger all emit.

stateSelectorChanges.from: group-required:block (label.tsx, asterisk fallback when isRequired is undefined)
stateSelectorChanges.reason: the old selector compiled to .group:is([data-rac][data-required], :not([data-rac]):required) *, i.e. the group element itself had to carry data-required (React Aria) or be natively required - impossible for a wrapper div, since Base UI puts required on the control and Field.Root/Field.Control emit no data-required. group-has-required compiles to .group:has(:is([data-rac][data-required], :not([data-rac]):required)) *, which matches the wrapper that contains a required control, covering both the native `required` attribute and Base UI's data-required families (verified in a browser: asterisk becomes visible with only the field's required state, no props).

crossUnitNotes: Label/HintText only associate inside a Base UI Field.Root (Field parts throw outside one, and Field.Root is the only provider of the label/description context in 1.8.0). Field components that migrate to NumberField.Root/OTPField.Root/Select.Root/Combobox.Root/Checkbox.Root/Radio.Root/Switch.Root should wrap them in Field.Root so the existing <Label>/<HintText> children keep their htmlFor/aria-labelledby/aria-describedby wiring; otherwise those components must switch to the family's own label part.

The `.group` element that the label/hint are inside is owned by the field components: for group-data-invalid to work it must be (or contain) a Base UI element that emits data-invalid - Field.Root, NumberField.Root, Select.Trigger, Combobox, Checkbox, Radio, Switch and OTPField all do; a plain <div> with only React Aria's isInvalid prop would not.

The migration harness has no Field.Root-based case for this unit; both of its cases (field-label-hint, field-invalid) render the standalone path. If the lead wants a permanent regression case for the association path, add a `Field.Root > Field.Label + Field.Control + Field.Description` case to src/migration-harness.tsx (not editable from this unit).
